Impartial Analysis - Measure M — Gilroy Unified School District — Bonds

ok / California law permits school districts to issue bonds with the approval of 55% of district voters.
Such bonds may be used only for construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, or replacement of

school facilities, including furnishing and equipping those facilities, or the acquisition or lease of
real property for school facilities.

The Board of Education (Board) of the Gilroy Unified School District (District) has placed on
the ballot a Measure authorizing the issuance and sale of up to $295 million in such bonds.

As identified in the Measure, projects may include but are not limited to:

e Replacing portable classrooms with permanent classrooms;

e Renovating, constructing, and/or modernizing classrooms for current educational
standards, including acquiring, installing, and/or upgrading technology equipment,
fixtures, and infrastructure;

e Reconfiguring, repairing, resurfacing, and/or expanding parking lots and related areas;

e Constructing, improving, and/or renovating restrooms;

e Modernizing, expanding, and/or upgrading classrooms, common areas, and school
support facilities such as libraries, multipurpose rooms, and cafeterias;

e Constructing, renovating, and/or acquiring and installing physical education facilities and
playfields;

e Removing, repairing, and refinishing building and site areas damaged by dry rot, water,
and termites;

e Making energy-efficiency upgrades;

e Repairing or replacing roofs; and

¢ Upgrading, constructing, and/or installing safety and security improvements such as
fencing, lighting, fire suppression systems, and emergency communication systems.

Bond proceeds may be spent on eligible project costs, such as planning and design, hazardous
materials sampling and removal, séismic evaluations, ‘furnishing school facilities, and all other

costs and works necessary or incidental to the listed bond projects. In accordance with state law,
the Measure states that bond proceeds would not be used for teacher or administrator salaries or
other school operating expenses.

These general obligation bonds will be payable from ad valorem taxes levied on taxable real
property within the District. The Measure states that the best estimate of the average annual tax
rate to be levied to repay the proposed bonds is $59.14 per $100,000 of assessed value, that the
final fiscal year in which the tax is anticipated to be collected will be 2059-2060, and that the
best estimate of the total debt service during the life of the bond, including principal and interest,
is $623.3 million.

and spend the proceeds only for these purposes. The stated purposes of the tax proposed by

e Enhance academic programs, core instruction, literacy, reading, mathematics, science, and

staff;

the parcel as a principal residence.

parcel on parcels within the District for seven years, beginning July 1, 2027.
